summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of common variable immunodeficiency, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma status post allogeneic stem cell transplant, and a colostomy presented with significant bleeding from her ostomy site, lasting several hours and causing fatigue and lightheadedness. Evaluation revealed the bleed originated at the skin-stoma junction, likely due to irritation and low platelets. She was treated with Surgicel and two units of platelets, which stopped the bleeding. Her diarrhea, which had been malodorous and watery, resolved during admission, and stool testing was negative for C. difficile and other pathogens. Tacrolimus dose was increased due to a subtherapeutic level. She remained stable, with no recurrence of bleeding or infection, and was discharged home with follow-up plans, a walker for gait instability, and instructions to avoid manipulating the stoma.
